title: JMoney: The Numbers Guy Still Waiting for the Numbers to Add Up
body: Jordan arrived in the Buckaroo Football League in 2026, part of the expansion class that took the league from six teams to eight. He showed up with Counting or not Counting GV, a team name that sounds like a spreadsheet arguing with itself, and a reputation as the guy who doesn't really know football but absolutely knows math. That's a bold strategy in a sport where the math keeps getting tackled by reality, and seven weeks into his career JMoney is learning that lesson the hard way.

The 2026 campaign has been a grind. Counting or not Counting GV sits at 1-6 with 622.5 points for, roughly 88.9 per week, and the title odds now read a clean, unarguable 0%. The low point came in week 7, when Ramon's No Banner only HULK held him to 60.9 points, a performance so quiet it barely registered on the scoreboard. For a man who loves numbers, that's one he'd probably like to delete from the dataset.

Then there's the high. In week 5, Jordan erupted for 119.7 points, his career best and his lone win, and he did it against Zoe and Ghostu-Spider SZN. Beating the rookie who's been locked in all season counts as a statement in any household, and his is officially 1-0 in head-to-head bragging rights. Everyone else has his number so far: he's 0-1 against Randy, Sonny, Alan, Mekhi, Kaushal and Ramon, which means six managers have a W in the JMoney column and are waiting to see who gets the first rematch.

As a manager, Jordan has been more active than his record suggests. He's swung one trade and worked the waiver wire for seven pickups, the kind of steady tinkering you'd expect from somebody who treats a roster like a problem set to be solved. The results haven't followed yet, but the willingness to keep adjusting is there, like a band kid running the same eight bars until they finally land.

Where does that leave him? Out of the title picture in year one, but with a 119.7-point ceiling on the books and a full slate of rematches to come. The rest of the league would be wise not to sleep on a guy who's already proven he can drop a big number on the right Sunday. JMoney's first season isn't over, and somewhere in his head the regression-to-the-mean chart is already being drawn.
